## Findings

I launched BenchTarget cold five times (force-stop + relaunch) on the Pixel 8 Pro (Android 16) and navigated Home → About → Diagnostics each time. The "Retry sync" button was visible on 3 runs and completely absent on 2 runs — reproducing the reported ~3/5 pass rate.

**Root cause: a persisted launch counter, not test/UI timing.**

Logcat (tag `BenchTarget`) shows `SyncComponent` logging its init state on every cold start:

| Cold-start # | `launchCount` | `skip` | Diagnostics screen |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | false | "Sync idle" + **Retry sync visible** |
| 2 | 1 | false | "Sync idle" + **Retry sync visible** |
| 3 | 2 | **true** | "Sync unavailable" + **no button at all** |
| 4 | 3 | false | "Sync idle" + **Retry sync visible** |
| 5 | 4 | **true** | "Sync unavailable" + **no button at all** |

`launchCount` is stored in SharedPreferences and survives force-stop/relaunch (I confirmed this — it kept incrementing across kills). It only resets to 0 after `pm clear` (app data wipe), which I verified directly: clearing app data and relaunching produced `launchCount=0 skip=false` again.

The `skip` flag (which the Diagnostics screen uses to decide whether to render "Sync idle" + the Retry sync button, vs. "Sync unavailable" with no button) is false for the first two launches, then flips to **true on every even `launchCount` from 2 onward** (2, 4, 6, …) and false on the odd ones in between. Over any run of 5 consecutive cold starts that lands on this part of the cycle, you get exactly 2 failures and 3 passes — matching the report precisely.

**Why it looks flaky:** the test only ever cold-launches the app and asserts the button is visible. It never accounts for the fact that BenchTarget's own launch count persists across app restarts on the device/emulator. So the "flakiness" isn't flaky at all — it's a deterministic function of how many times the app has been cold-started since its data was last cleared, which drifts silently across test runs (and across different tests sharing the same installed app) unless data is wiped before each run.

**Fix direction:** either (a) have the test call `pm clear`/uninstall-reinstall before each run so `launchCount` always starts at 0, or (b) if this behavior is intentional simulated flakiness in BenchTarget (per its "About" text, it's a benchmark target for reproducible agent runs), the test needs to account for the skip cycle rather than assert unconditional visibility — e.g., assert on the Sync status text/branch rather than assuming the button is always present.
